title: Androgenic (anabolic) steroid use causes severe acne
vignette: An 18-year-old man comes to the office due to acne. The patient has had mild facial acne for the past 3 years that has responded well to topical agents. Since he started college 2 months ago, the acne has worsened and has spread to his torso and neck. Despite use of the topical agents, it has continued to worsen. The patient plays on the university's baseball team, which requires him to practice outdoors for several hours 3 days a week. He also swims in an indoor pool several hours a week. Since starting college, the patient has adopted a dairy-free, low-glycemic-index diet. Physical examination shows severe, nodulocystic acne on the face, neck, chest, and back. Which of the following most likely caused this patient's worsening acne?

clues.text: acne has worsened and has spread to his torso and neck
clues.note: Rapid worsening and spread beyond the face to the trunk (chest/back) suggests a new systemic androgenic drive rather than routine topical-responsive acne.

clues.text: plays on the university's baseball team
clues.note: A competitive athlete is a demographic where anabolic-androgenic steroid use should be considered as a cause of sudden severe acne.

clues.text: severe, nodulocystic acne on the face, neck, chest, and back
clues.note: Sudden severe nodulocystic acne over androgen-sensitive areas (face, chest, back) is a hallmark of androgenic (anabolic) steroid supplementation.

whatMatters: An athlete with sudden, SEVERE nodulocystic acne spreading to the trunk despite topical therapy and a diet change points to ANDROGENIC (anabolic) STEROID SUPPLEMENTATION (methyltestosterone). Androgens increase sebum production and follicular hyperproliferation, driving acne. Answer D. The diet and pool/UV exposures don't cause this.
strategy: Recognize the pattern: competitive athlete + explosive nodulocystic acne on androgen-sensitive skin = exogenous androgens. Reject the red-herring lifestyle factors: a dairy-free/low-glycemic diet would IMPROVE (not worsen) acne; chlorinated water tends to improve acne (antibacterial); UV radiation causes photodermatoses, not sudden severe acne.

eliminations.label: Dairy-free diet - would improve, not worsen acne
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: avoiding dairy (skim milk is associated with acne). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: removing dairy would tend to IMPROVE acne, not worsen it. ✅ Correct if: asking what dietary change might HELP acne.

eliminations.label: Chlorinated water - antibacterial, tends to improve acne
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: chlorine exposure from an indoor pool. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: chlorine has antibacterial effects against Cutibacterium acnes and generally improves, not worsens, acne. ✅ Correct if: asking about a factor that could reduce acne bacteria.

eliminations.label: Low-glycemic-index diet - improves acne
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a low-glycemic diet (lower insulin/IGF-1). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: low-glycemic diets are associated with LESS acne, so this would help, not harm. ✅ Correct if: asking about a beneficial dietary change.

eliminations.label: UV radiation - photodermatoses, not severe acne
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: sun/UV exposure. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: UV can cause sunburn or drug-induced photosensitivity but does not cause sudden severe nodulocystic acne. ✅ Correct if: a photosensitivity reaction (e.g., on tetracyclines).

reasoning: Competitive athlete with sudden severe nodulocystic acne spreading to the trunk despite topicals
This pattern suggests a new systemic androgenic stimulus
Androgens (anabolic steroids) increase sebum production and follicular hyperproliferation -> acne
mechanism: Androgens (endogenous testosterone/DHEA or exogenous anabolic-androgenic steroids such as methyltestosterone) are central to acne pathogenesis: they bind receptors in sebaceous glands, increasing SEBUM production, and promote follicular epidermal HYPERPROLIFERATION, obstructing the pilosebaceous unit. The trapped sebum is metabolized by Cutibacterium acnes with release of inflammatory mediators, and follicular rupture produces inflammatory and nodulocystic lesions. The androgen-acne link is evident at puberty and in hyperandrogenic states (e.g., polycystic ovary syndrome). When a young athlete suddenly develops severe nodulocystic acne over androgen-sensitive areas (face, chest, back), exogenous ANDROGENIC (anabolic) STEROID use should be strongly suspected. The other listed exposures do not explain worsening: dairy-free and low-glycemic diets are associated with LESS acne (lower insulin/IGF-1), chlorinated water is antibacterial and tends to improve acne, and UV radiation causes sunburn/photodermatoses rather than sudden severe acne.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Derm/Pharm > acne pathogenesis: androgens -> ↑sebum + follicular hyperproliferation + C. acnes; anabolic-androgenic steroid use causes sudden severe/nodulocystic acne (acne fulminans).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Athlete + explosive nodulocystic trunk acne = exogenous androgens, not diet/pool/UV.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on nodulocystic acne, sebum, follicular hyperproliferation, Cutibacterium acnes, or anabolic-androgenic steroids? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Dairy-free + low-glycemic diets IMPROVE acne; chlorinated water is antibacterial (improves); UV causes photodermatoses, not acne.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: androgens drive acne (↑sebum + follicular hyperproliferation); suspect anabolic steroids in athletes with sudden severe acne.
